config.title: Write a debounce utility

intro.title: Write a debounce utility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a debounce utility function in JavaScript, which helps delay the execution of a function until after a specified wait time has passed without new calls. You'll learn the core programming concept of debouncing, a technique used to optimize performance by preventing a function from being called too frequently, such as during rapid user input like typing or scrolling. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, closures, and timers like setTimeout and clearTimeout. By the end, you'll have a reusable debounce function that can control how often a function runs, improving application efficiency.
intro.usecase: Debouncing is essential in real-world applications where user interactions trigger frequent events that could overwhelm systems. In search interfaces, debouncing prevents excessive API calls as users type queries, improving performance and reducing server load. Similarly, window resize handlers use debouncing to recalculate layouts efficiently without causing janky UI updates. Form validation and dashboard filter controls also benefit by delaying execution until users pause interaction, creating smoother experiences.

objectives: Construct a debounce function that accepts a callback and a delay parameter.
Initialize a timer variable to manage the delay execution.
Manipulate the timer to clear and reset it on repeated calls.
Apply the debounce utility to control a button click handler.
Integrate the debounce function to prevent rapid API calls from an input field.
Configure the debounce delay to adjust the waiting period.
Implement a leading-edge option to execute the callback immediately on the first call.

steps.title: Create a function skeleton for debounce
steps.instruction: Create a function called 'debounce' that takes two parameters: 'func' and 'delay'.
steps.hint: Start by writing the function signature. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named debounce with two parameters (func and delay) is created.
successCriteria: The code defines a function named 'debounce' that accepts 'func' and 'delay' as parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named 'debounce' and takes two parameters: 'func' and 'delay'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a function called 'debounce' that accepts two parameters: 'func' and 'delay'.

steps.title: Initialize a timeout variable
steps.instruction: Inside your debounce function, declare a variable called timeoutId to store the timeout reference.
steps.hint: You can use let to declare a variable that will be reassigned later.
steps.expectedOutcome: The debounce function now has a timeoutId variable ready to store timeout references.
successCriteria: A variable named timeoutId is declared inside the debounce function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've declared a variable called timeoutId inside the debounce function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The timeoutId variable hasn't been declared yet. Add a variable declaration inside the debounce function.

steps.title: Return the debounced function
steps.instruction: Inside your debounce function, return a new function that will serve as the debounced version.
steps.hint: The debounce function should return a function expression or arrow function. You can start with `return function() {}` or `return () => {}`.
steps.expectedOutcome: The debounce function now returns a new function, which will later contain the debounced logic.
successCriteria: The debounce function returns a function (either function expression or arrow function).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a function from the debounce function. Check that you have a return statement followed by a function definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The debounce function should return a new function. Try adding `return function() {}` or `return () => {}` inside the debounce function body.

steps.title: Capture arguments in the returned function
steps.instruction: Inside the returned function in your debounce function, add a parameter using rest syntax to capture all arguments passed to it.
steps.hint: Use the rest parameter syntax (...args) to collect all arguments into an array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The returned function will have a parameter that collects all arguments passed to it.
successCriteria: The returned function has a rest parameter (e.g., ...args) to capture arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the rest parameter syntax (...args) in the returned function's parameter list.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. The returned function needs a parameter that collects all arguments using rest syntax.

steps.title: Clear previous timeout
steps.instruction: Inside the returned function, use clearTimeout to cancel any existing timeout before setting a new one.
steps.hint: Call clearTimeout with the timeoutId variable as its argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The debounced function will now clear any pending timeout before scheduling a new one, preventing multiple executions.
successCriteria: The returned function includes a clearTimeout call with timeoutId as the argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling clearTimeout with the timeoutId variable inside the returned function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires clearing the timeout. Use clearTimeout(timeoutId) inside the returned function.

steps.title: Set new timeout
steps.instruction: Inside the returned function, set a new timeout that will call the original function with the captured arguments after the specified delay.
steps.hint: Use setTimeout to schedule the original function call. Pass the captured arguments to the original function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The debounced function will schedule the original function to be called after the delay, using the captured arguments.
successCriteria: A setTimeout call is added inside the returned function that calls the original function with the captured arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling the original function with the captured arguments inside setTimeout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The timeout wasn't set correctly. Remember to use setTimeout to schedule the function call with the captured arguments.

steps.title: Create a test function to debounce
steps.instruction: Create a simple function named 'logMessage' that logs 'Button clicked!' to the console. This will be used to test your debounce utility.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses console.log() to output a message. You can place it after your debounce function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'logMessage' is created that logs a message to the console when called.
successCriteria: The code contains a function named 'logMessage' that uses console.log() to output 'Button clicked!'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named 'logMessage' and logs exactly 'Button clicked!' to the console.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test function is missing or doesn't match the requirements. Create a function named 'logMessage' that logs 'Button clicked!' to the console.

steps.title: Apply debounce to the test function
steps.instruction: Call your debounce function with your test function and a delay of 300 milliseconds, storing the returned debounced version in a variable named debouncedTest.
steps.hint: Invoke debounce() with two arguments: your test function and the number 300, then assign the result to a variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: applying a utility to a function
const throttledLog = throttle(console.log, 200);
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a debounced version of your test function ready to use.
successCriteria: The debounce function is called with your test function and 300, and the result is stored in a variable named debouncedTest.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling debounce() with your test function and 300, and storing the result in a variable named debouncedTest.
steps.feedbackWrong: call debounce() with your test function and a delay of 300, then store the returned function in a variable named debouncedTest.

steps.title: Test the debounced function with rapid calls
steps.instruction: Call the debounced function multiple times in quick succession to observe debounce behavior.
steps.hint: Write several consecutive calls to your debounced function, separated by commas or on separate lines.
steps.expectedOutcome: The debounced function should only execute once after the delay when called rapidly multiple times.
successCriteria: The debounced function is called at least three times in quick succession.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to call the debounced function multiple times in quick succession.
steps.feedbackWrong: The debounced function needs to be called multiple times to demonstrate the debounce behavior.

steps.title: Test with different arguments
steps.instruction: Call the debounced test function with different arguments to verify they are passed correctly to the original function.
steps.hint: Invoke debouncedTest with various arguments like strings or numbers. The original testFunction will log them when executed after the delay.
steps.expectedOutcome: The debounced function should be called with various arguments, and after the 300ms delay, the original testFunction should execute with those arguments.
successCriteria: debouncedTest is called at least twice with different arguments, such as strings or numbers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've called the debounced function, but try adding at least two calls with different arguments to fully test the argument passing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The debounced function wasn't called with different arguments. Ensure you invoke debouncedTest with varying values like 'hello' and 42.
